source.title: Elucidating the design space of language models for image generation
source.authors: Xuan-Tong Liu; Shaozhe Hao; Xianbiao Qi; Tianyang Hu; Jun Wang; Rong Xiao; Yuan Yao

record.file_problem: The full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It extends scaling analysis to autoregressive image generation and reports training-loss behavior across model sizes, a new modality relative to text pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study reports no fitted power-law exponents, small-run extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its image-generation FID results are recorded under fits_no_version because they are not held-out pretraining loss or downstream-task results. Attention visualizations and tokenizer reconstruction results do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: It reports training loss across four autoregressive image-model sizes (L, XL, XXL, 2B) on ImageNet tokens (Fig. 9), a new modality. This bears weakly on V5. It fits no power law and reports no exponents, and the sizes span less than one order of magnitude (about 0.3B to 1.9B).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim AR image models show a strong scaling law, citing lower training loss, better FID and more global attention with size. They explain the gains by larger models capturing global context. They fit no law and report no exponents.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains AR transformers to generate discretized ImageNet images, rather than measuring held-out text-pretraining loss; it reports size-related loss trends but no power-law fitting or extrapolation.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size and tokenizer/decomposition choice affect reported training loss and image-generation performance; the 2B loss run was stopped earlier than the others.

fits_no_version.finding: Generation FID improves with model size for ELM models (2.17 to 1.54) and for AR models at fixed tokenizers (Table 9). MLM FID plateaus from XL to XXL (3.13 to 3.12, Table 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Image-generation quality (FID) of language-model image generators improves with parameter count, more reliably for AR than MLM.

fits_no_version.finding: The best tokenizer vocabulary grows with model size (2-10 is best for L and XL, 2-12 for XXL).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimal vocabulary size grows with model size in AR image generation.

record.problems: The scaling-loss evidence is presented as a figure without numeric loss values or uncertainty estimates; the 2B run stopped earlier due to time constraints. No power-law fits, exponents, or held-out-loss results are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows left out. Other training-loss comparisons in Figure 10 concern tokenizer decomposition rather than the claim versions; tokenizer and attention analyses are not held-out loss scaling results.

untested.parts: The power-law form, exponents, and any fit. Scaling in data or compute (data fixed at ImageNet). Held-out loss. Video, fine-tuning and transfer regimes.
All parts (no text LM loss scaling).
All parts; depth and width change together with size.
All parts; FID is generation quality, not a downstream task.

missing.what: FID across sizes at fixed tokenizer: AR vs MLM (Table 8) and AR per tokenizer (Table 9). These are cleaner size sweeps than the ELM rows.

record.verdict_notes: Weak evidence: four sizes spanning under 10x, training (not held-out) loss after 400 repeated epochs, and figure-only values. The 2B run was truncated. Tokenizer choice is confounded with size in the ELM rows.

versions.untested_parts: Text-language-model held-out pretraining loss across parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Controlled comparisons of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.

The study reports image-domain training-loss trends across model sizes, but does not fit or establish a power-law form, report exponents, test other modalities, or test repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer regimes.
Downstream-task performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices, and systematic departures from single power laws.

relation.reason: The study reports its own size-dependent training-loss results and explicitly examines scaling behavior; its evidence is insufficient to establish a power law.

tranche.reason: The image-token model-size/training-loss comparison is a new setting bearing weakly on V5, although it cannot resolve the claimed functional form.

source_check.notes: The authors describe a strong scaling law but provide no power-law fit or exponents. Table 2 contains the method's generation-quality comparisons, with tokenizers changing across sizes; these are not direct evidence for V5.
